place: Sandersville, Georgia -- Washington County, the Kaolin Capital of the World (~2.5hr southeast of Atlanta)

city_center.name: Downtown Sandersville courthouse square
city_center.landmark: Washington County Courthouse (built 1868-69, High Victorian with a Second Empire clock tower carrying a Seth Thomas clock; enlarged 1899) at the center of the town square, ringed by turn-of-the-century brick storefronts
city_center.notes: Sandersville is the Washington County seat (pop ~5,800, 2020). Two downtown fires (1855, 1864 -- the latter during Sherman's march) destroyed the wooden commercial core; brick store buildings replaced the wood before 1900, giving the square its current 19th-c brick character. The Sandersville downtown farmers market runs off the square. sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandersville,_Georgia; sandersvillega.org/history.cfm; digitalcommons.unf.edu (courthouse 1868-69, Second Empire clock tower); dlg.usg.edu (fires 1855/1864, brick replaced wood); achp.gov Preserve America Sandersville.

cultural_notes: Washington County was created by the Georgia legislature in 1784 as land grants rewarding Revolutionary War veterans; it was the ninth Georgia county and the first county in the nation named for General George Washington, and Sandersville was the first US city named for him (source: sandersvillega.org/kaolincapitaloftheworld.cfm; wacohistorical.org/history)

Sandersville is the 'Kaolin Capital of the World' -- Washington County's deposits of white aluminosilicate kaolin clay are unusually pure, white, and easily mined; Georgia mines roughly $1 billion of kaolin a year, more than any other state (source: earthobservatory.nasa.gov Kaolin Capital of the World, citing USGS; sandersvillega.org)

the Sandersville Railroad, a shortline nicknamed 'The Kaolin Road,' was built 1893-94 to move fine white clay and drove the town's 1890-1910 growth (source: sandersvillega.org/sandersville-railroad.cfm; achp.gov Preserve America)

farm heritage runs deep: Washington County agriculture is led by timber, beef, and corn with over $70 million in farm gate value, alongside pecans, muscadine, and sweet potatoes -- a genuine working farm county, treated respectfully as a living community, not a nostalgia prop (source: UGA extension Washington County annual report; extension.uga.edu)

Georgia is 'the Peach State' and a top-three US pecan producer; muscadine, the native Southern grape, peaks Aug-Sep and pecans at the November harvest (source: UGA extension crop calendar framing; retailer-frontier-pairs.json monthly_ingredient_notes)

sweet-onion note handled carefully: true Vidalia onions are a Georgia certification mark restricted to a 20-county southeast-Georgia zone centered on Toombs and Tattnall counties -- Washington County is NOT in that legal zone, so local sweet onions are framed as 'Vidalia-adjacent' Granex-type, never labeled Vidalia (source: agr.georgia.gov Vidalia Onion Act of 1986; fieldreport.caes.uga.edu 'Toombs and Tattnall are the heart of Vidalia onion country'; gardenandgun.com peak late May-June)

the courthouse square's 19th-c brick storefronts replaced wooden buildings lost to the 1855 and 1864 fires -- the built environment is red brick over white kaolin ground, a distinctive brown-on-white palette signature (source: dlg.usg.edu; sandersvillega.org/history.cfm)
